title: Proposal: templates as functions
body:
Today templates can be:

* strings, automatically passed to Hogan (inlined in the library)
* functions that must return strings (not passed to Hogan)
* React stateless components (because why not)

This adds some good complexity, both in term of user facing API but also in terms of internal implementation.

The templating system is spread accross the whole codebase, Hogan helpers goes from instantsearch(option) down to the rendering.

Since the introduction of [template literals](https://developer.mozilla.org/en/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Template_literals) we can now have easy templates in JavaScript.

But those are compatible only with latest browsers (Chrome, FF, Edge, iOS >= 9).

And not everyone would be happy using template literals. So we would still need to document how to use another templating system.

I propose to:

* keep only templates as functions returning strings in the core
* advocate for the use of template functions (no template literals)
* have a clear templating guide
  * how to use template literals with instantsearch.js
  * how to use Hogan with instantsearch.js
  * possibly others
* maybe be able to create templating plugins to easily use Hogan
